summary: Renames the Django User.note DB column to customer_note while preserving the public GraphQL field name note. Adds a nullable customer_note column, backfills existing note values, adds PostgreSQL triggers to synchronize note and customer_note columns during concurrent dual-version operation, deploys the new version with a state-only migration, retires the old version, and finally drops the note column after cleanup of dependent triggers and function.
write_consistency: The expand phase adds customer_note alongside note. The backfill copies all existing note values into customer_note, preserving NULLs. The sync stage adds BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE INSERT triggers with FOR EACH ROW WHEN conditions that mirror writes between note and customer_note, ensuring either version's writes are visible to the other version's reads, including at INSERT time. The note column remains active for the old version through the deploy_new and retire_old stages; it is dropped only after retire_old when the old version no longer serves traffic, with associated triggers and function cleaned up first to avoid reference errors.
revision_notes: Modified contract_1 stage sql to drop the sync_user_note() function and all four triggers before executing ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note CASCADE. Root cause: the contract_1 stage dropped the note column while the sync_user_note() function and INSERT triggers still referenced it, causing ProgrammingError: record new has no field note when triggers fired on INSERT. Adding explicit DROP TRIGGER and DROP FUNCTION statements before the column removal prevents residual trigger activation.

stages.description: Add the customer_note column to the account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note for all rows.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Add PostgreSQL triggers to synchronize note and customer_note columns during concurrent dual-version operation.
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_user_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; ELSIF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_note BEFORE UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note) EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note();
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_customer_note BEFORE UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note) EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note();
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_note_insert BEFORE INSERT ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note();
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_customer_note_insert BEFORE INSERT ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new-staged version with a state_only Django migration (no SQL); the schema change is already applied by the SQL stages above.
Retire the old version. After this stage only the new version runs, which exclusively uses customer_note.
Remove the old note column after the old version is retired and dependent triggers/function are cleaned up.
sql: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sync_note_insert ON account_user;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sync_customer_note_insert ON account_user;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sync_note ON account_user;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sync_customer_note ON account_user;
ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note CASCADE;
